newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Two Malaysia shows for Jackson after ban lifted.
newsitem.headline: Two Malaysia shows for Jackson after ban lifted.

text.p: Pop star Michael Jackson, told he was unwelcome in a Malaysian state two weeks ago, will now be allowed to stage two concerts in the capital Kuala Lumpur, the national Bernama news agency reported on Monday.

Jackson was originally scheduled to do a single show at the Shah Alam stadium in central Selangor state on October 27 until state authorities abruptly banned the concert, saying the singer would have an undesirable effect on local youth.

Malaysia's federal government ignored the Selangor decision last week and welcomed Jackson to Kuala Lumpur's Merdeka Stadium. Minister of Culture Sabbaruddin Chik went a step further on Monday, saying the singer could do another show on October 29.
"We've been told that all the tickets are nearly sold out. So the government is allowing another day," Sabbaruddin was quoted as saying by Bernama.
He said the extra show was to make up for the Merdeka Stadium's limited capacity of 40,000 compared to Shah Alam's 80,000.
Jackson has a wide following in this predominantly Moslem country, where he has never perfomed. Tickets for his performance are priced between 65 and 350 ringgit ($26 and $140).
